questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Slots in an electric motor rotor
questions.learningObjective: Explain what slots in a motor rotor accomplish electromagnetically.
questions.stem: A transit board asks why slots are cut in a motor rotor core.

options.text: Slots reduce eddy currents and guide flux in the rotor core.
Slots exist only to reduce rotor mass.
options.misconception: thinks slots are for mass reduction

options.text: Slots create permanent magnets in the core.
Slots prevent any current in the rotor.

questions.explanation: Slots reduce eddy-current losses and help flux; they are not for mass, magnetization, or eliminating current.
questions.hint: Think about eddy currents and flux paths.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Inductance of a toroid from its flux
questions.learningObjective: Explain how inductance follows from flux linkage and current.
questions.stem: A toroid has 500 turns, flux 0.002 Wb, current 10 A; find inductance in henries.
questions.explanation: Inductance equals flux linkage divided by current; 500 times 0.002 Wb is 1 Wb-turn, divided by 10 A gives 0.1 H.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Current transformer's burden and current ratio

Secondary current is primary current scaled by the turns ratio.
Secondary current is primary divided by burden resistance.
Burden voltage does not affect secondary current.

questions.explanation: The CT scales current by the turns ratio; burden resistance affects voltage, not the ideal current ratio.
questions.hint: Use the turns ratio, not resistance.

questions.topic: Where the heat comes from in induction heating
questions.learningObjective: Explain the source of heat in induction heating.
questions.stem: Eddy current 7 A, resistance 2 ohm; heating power in watts?
questions.explanation: I squared R gives 49 times 2, so 98 W from eddy-current heating.
questions.hint: Square current and multiply by resistance.

questions.topic: Field inside a toroid
questions.learningObjective: Explain the magnetic field inside a toroid.
questions.stem: A toroid has 250 turns, 2 A, radius 0.1 m; field inside in tesla?
questions.explanation: B equals 2e-7 N I over r, giving 0.001 T. The field is circumferential inside the toroid.

questions.topic: What the Curie temperature marks
questions.learningObjective: Explain what the Curie temperature marks in a ferromagnet.
questions.stem: A transit board lists a Curie temperature of 420 C; convert it to kelvin?
questions.explanation: Add 273.15 to 420 to obtain 693.15 K. Above this temperature ferromagnetic order is lost.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Slots in an electric motor rotor
questions.learningObjective: Explain what slots in a motor rotor accomplish electromagnetically.
questions.stem: The purpose of rotor slots is...

options.text: Slots exist only to reduce rotor mass.
options.misconception: thinks slots are for mass reduction

options.text: Slots create permanent magnets in the core.
Slots reduce eddy currents and guide flux in the rotor core.
Slots prevent any current in the rotor.

questions.explanation: Slots reduce eddy-current losses and help flux; they are not for mass, magnetization, or eliminating current.
questions.hint: Think about eddy currents and flux paths.

questions.topic: Inductance of a toroid from its flux
questions.learningObjective: Explain how inductance follows from flux linkage and current.
questions.stem: Flux 0.008 Wb, 200 turns, current 10 A; inductance in henries?
questions.explanation: Flux linkage 1.6 divided by 10 A gives 0.16 H. Geometry is encoded in the flux.
questions.hint: Multiply turns by flux, then divide by current.

questions.topic: A steady field induces no current in a conductor
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a steady field induces no current.
questions.stem: A conductor in a steady 3.0 T field; induced emf in volts?
questions.explanation: A steady field means constant flux, so Faraday's law gives zero induced emf; motion or field change is needed.
questions.hint: Check whether the flux is changing.
